STATUS: fail
SUMMARY: Two reproduced correctness bugs with the flag on. A target that is itself a shadow host gets its own shadow content hidden, and a slot added inside an already-hidden wrapper leaves the projected target hidden. The nested, out-of-order, refcount, root-option and light-DOM observer paths held up under probing. Both probe files are deleted and `git status` matches the start.

FILES TOUCHED: none (probe files `zzProbe*.test.js` were created in packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/ and deleted)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Target that is a shadow host: `addShadowPath` starts at the target itself and adds `target.shadowRoot` to the walked set, so the host's own internal content is hidden. Reproduced: a `<div>` with an open shadow root containing a `<button>`, passed as the target. `expect(btn).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden')` fails with `aria-hidden="true"`. The same happens when the host is in light DOM (P1b). Breaks "hosts on the path stay visible" and hides a target's own UI from AT.
- [blocking] Slot added into an already-hidden wrapper: the observer skips `change.target` because it is in `hiddenNodes`, so the slot's ancestors are never revealed even though the recomputed `slots` set now covers them. Reproduced: wrapper `div` in shadow root (hidden at call time), target light child of host, then `append(wrapper, 'slot')`. `expect(wrapper).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden')` fails with `aria-hidden="true"`, so the projected target is hidden from AT.
- [minor] The `shouldUseInert: true` path is not exercised. jsdom has no `inert` on `HTMLElement.prototype`, so `supportsInert` is false and the probe ran on aria-hidden. The acceptance criterion is unverified under inert.
- [minor] Test-order coupling: the flag-off test relies on running before `beforeAll(enableShadowDOM)` in the same file, and there is no flag-off isolation.

CHECKS:
- P1 target is a shadow host (in shadow root and light DOM) → FAIL (blocking)
- P2 slot added inside hidden wrapper, target projected → FAIL (blocking)
- P3 target 2 levels deep, sibling host gets late shadow content → pass
- P4 out-of-order cleanup, targets in two shadow roots, late additions to each → pass
- P6 refcount: two calls hiding the same shadow sibling, cleanup order → pass
- P7 `root` inside a shadow root, siblings above root untouched → pass
- P8 `keepVisible` on an element inside a shadow root → pass
- P9 content added inside a hidden sibling in a shadow root is not separately hidden; cleanup restores → pass
- Q1 deep addition into a visible path wrapper in an enclosing root → hidden; path host visible → pass
- Q3 text node plus element added to a shadow root → no throw, element hidden → pass
- Q4 target slotted through a slot in an enclosing root: slot, wrapper and host visible; sibling and light sibling hidden; cleanup restores → pass
- Q5 slot removed mid-flight, then cleanup → no error, sibling restored → pass
- Q6 target removed, then cleanup → sibling restored → pass
- Q7 `root` equal to a shadow host → pass
- Q9 new host with shadow root added to a root after the call → host hidden, its shadow content not hidden → pass
- P5, P6b, Q2, Q8: failed only because my expectations were wrong (not code defects). P5: the outer call correctly hides the new sibling of its own. Q2: the content was under an already-hidden parent. Q8: `s2` is correctly unhidden after the inner cleanup. P6b: jsdom lacks inert, so `sib.inert` is undefined.
- Flag-off with a shadow-hosted target: `body` itself is hidden because `nodeContains` is plain `contains`. This matches the pre-existing behavior, so not a regression.
- The existing flag-off test in `ariaHideOutside.test.js` covers flag-off behavior; I did not re-run it.

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should the target-as-host case (P1) exclude the target's own shadow root from the walk? The fix for P1 and P2 is the author's call. Re-review should re-run P1, P1b and P2 after the change.
